Bash(git commit -m "$(cat <<''EOF''
Add SvelteKit frontend with customizable range settings for hardware monitoring

This commit introduces a complete SvelteKit-based PWA frontend for real-time PC hardware monitoring with the following features:

- Real-time temperature and power monitoring for CPU and GPU
- Auto-refresh every 5 seconds fetching data from Upstash Redis Streams
- Responsive card-based UI with Tailwind CSS styling
- Dynamic status indicators with color-coded pulsing dots
- Customizable range settings for each metric via modal interface
- Progress bars with adjustable min/max ranges persisted to localStorage
- Enter key support for quick range updates
- PC name display and last update timestamp

Components:
- TemperatureCard: Displays CPU/GPU temperature with customizable ranges
- PowerCard: Displays CPU/GPU power consumption with customizable ranges
- RangeSettingsModal: Reusable modal for editing metric ranges
- StatusIndicator: Connection status with PC name and update time

The range customization feature allows users to set custom min/max values for each metric''s progress bar, making it easier to visualize values within specific operating ranges.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)")

Bash(git commit -m "$(cat <<''EOF''
Add configurable refresh interval and improved UI feedback

Backend changes:
- Increased data upload interval from 5s to 10s to reduce API usage

Frontend changes:
- Added RefreshSettingsModal component for customizable refresh intervals
- Changed from setInterval to setTimeout for accurate timing (waits for response before scheduling next refresh)
- Added manual refresh button with spinning animation during updates
- Updated StatusIndicator to show "Updating..." instead of "Loading..."
- Added live countdown timer that updates every second showing "Xs ago"
- Fixed negative time display issue with Math.max(0, diff)
- Default refresh interval set to 30 seconds (persisted to localStorage)
- Quick preset buttons for common intervals (5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, 60s)
- Warning note about API usage limits

New features:
- Global settings icon in header to configure refresh interval
- Manual refresh button that resets the auto-refresh timer
- Real-time "Updated Xs ago" counter
- Refresh cycle restarts after API response completes, not at fixed intervals

Monthly API usage (with defaults):
- Backend: 10s = ~259,200 commands/month
- Frontend: 30s = ~86,400 commands/month
- Total: ~345,600 commands/month (well within 500k free tier limit)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)")

Bash(git commit -m "$(cat <<''EOF''
Restructure project with backend/frontend separation and comprehensive documentation

Major changes:
- Moved backend files (main.go, go.mod, go.sum) to backend/ directory
- Added metrics-config.json for flexible metric extraction system
- Created comprehensive CLAUDE.md development guide
- Created user-friendly README.md with emojis and detailed setup instructions
- Added run.ps1 PowerShell launcher script

Backend improvements:
- Config-based metric extraction using JSON path definitions
- Support for dual CPU temperature monitoring (Tctl and CCD1)
- Automatic .env file loading with godotenv
- Pattern matching with | separator for hardware name alternatives
- Enhanced logging for all metric values

Frontend updates:
- Simplified data access with direct property references
- Updated to display both CPU temperatures (Tctl and CCD1)
- Changed temperature grid to 3 columns
- Created proper TypeScript interfaces in frontend/src/lib/types/
- Removed tree traversal logic (150+ lines eliminated)

Documentation:
- CLAUDE.md: 500+ line comprehensive guide with architecture, setup, troubleshooting
- README.md: User-friendly guide with emojis, quick start, features, roadmap
- Both files include step-by-step instructions for adding new metrics
